text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on March 17 in history:
45BC - Julius Caesar heavily defeated the Pompeians at the battle of Munda in Spain. The Pompeians, led by two sons of Pompey the Great, lost over 30,000 men.
180 - Marcus Aurelius, Roman Emperor, died. Sole emperor from 161, he defeated a German invasion of Italy but is best remembered for his "Meditations" on Stoic Philosophy.
1337 - Edward III created the Duchy of Cornwall for his eldest son Edward, who was later made Prince of Wales.
1776 - Having seized Dorchester Heights, George Washington forced the British under William Howe to evacuate Boston.
1834 - Gottlieb Daimler, German engineer, born. He was significant in the development of the internal combustion engine and founded the Daimler Automobile Company in 1890.
1860 - In New Zealand, the second Maori war broke out.
1861 - A new united kingdom of Italy was proclaimed by parliament with Victor Emmanuel II as King.
1912 - Lawrence Oates, English polar explorer with Scott's expedition to the Antarctic, left the tent on his 32nd birthday saying "I am just going outside, and may be some time". He never returned.
1919 - Nat "King" Cole, U.S. singer and entertainer, born. Originally a jazz pianist, he gained huge popularity as a singer with the songs "Mona Lisa", "Unforgettable" and "When I Fall in Love".
1929 - In Spain, the University of Madrid was closed by the government after student protests and rioting.
1938 - Rudolf Nureyev, Russian ballet dancer, born. Considered one of the 20th Century's great ballet dancers, he defected to the West in 1961.
1939 - British Prime Minister Chamberlain accused Adolf Hitler of breaking his word, after German troops crossed the Czech frontier.
1944 - Allied bombing on Austria began with a raid by over 200 planes on targets in Vienna.
1948 - The Brussels Treaty, a 50-year alliance between Britain, France and the Benelux countries, was signed to provide for military co-operation in the event of an attack.
1958 - The second U.S. satellite to orbit the Earth, Vanguard I, was launched from Cape Canaveral.
1960 - The second United Nations conference on the Law of the Sea opened in Geneva attended by 88 states. It ended on April 26 without agreement.
1963 - On Bali, the volcano Mount Agung erupted, killing at least 11,000 people.
1968 - Violent demonstrations against the Vietnam war erupted outside the American embassy in London. Over 300 arrests were made and 90 policemen injured.
1968 - A central bank governors' meeting in Washington agreed on a two-tier gold system.
1969 - Golda Meir was sworn in as prime minister of Israel.
1978 - The oil tanker Amoco Cadiz ran aground off the coast of Brittany, spilling 220,000 tonnes of oil.
1982 - Zimbabwean Prime Minister Robert Mugabe ordered the writing of a new constitution to replace that drawn up at the Lancaster House conference in London.
1995 - President Haydar Aliyev of Azerbaijan survived a coup attempt when troops crushed a revolt by an elite police unit led by Deputy Interior Minister Rovshan Javadov.
1995 - Ronald Kray, legendary half of British gangsters the Kray twins, died.
